key_concepts: Baking a Flat Texture from Multiple Materials.

content: Develop your mesh as normal, and applying materials (Image 1). In the UV workspace, select your mesh and [k]UV > Smart UV Project[/k] to unwrap your mesh (Image 2). In the Shading workspace, create a new image. In each separate material's network, add an [k]Image Texture[/k] node using a new image, 1024x1024 (Image 3). Do not connect the node to anything, and copy it into all other materials, leaving the [k]Image Texture[/k] as the active node in the network (Image 4). In the Render Properties tab, change the Render Engine to Cycles (Image 5). Under the Bake tab, change the Bake Type to Diffuse (if using Principled BSDF for your materials; if you are using Emission nodes, change the type to Emission), uncheck Direct and Indirect, and Bake (Image 6). In the UV workspace, with the baked image open, [k]Image > Save As[/k] and save the texture as a PNG file (Image 7). In the Shading workspace, remove all materials. Add a new material, and in its network remove the [k]Principled BSDF[/k] node and add in an [k]Image Texture[/k] node and an [k]Emission[/k] node (Image 8). This makes the object display your baked texture at full, flat brightness regardless of scene lighting — matching exactly how it'll look with an Unshaded material in Godot, so what you see in Blender's viewport is what you'll get in-game. Export your mesh as a GLB (Image 9).

Copy your GLB into the appropriate Godot project folder. After the Godot Engine imports your mesh, double-click the glb file and from the Import Setting window set [k]Materials > Extract > Extract Once[/k] and [k]Materials > Extract Path[/k] to the folder path where you will store materials. Press [k]ReImport[/k]. Drag the .glb file from FileSystem into your scene tree and click the [k]Open in Editor[/k] button (Image 10). In the scene tree, expand the instance down to the MeshInstance3D node. Select it, go to the Inspector, find the [k]Mesh → Surface Material Override[/k] slot. Create a new [k]StandardMaterial3D[/k]. Scroll to [k]Shading[/k] section and set [k]Shading Mode → Unshaded[/k]. Point the [k]Albedo → Texture[/k] slot to your baked texture. If you want a toon outliner, under [k]Next Pass[/k], add a new [k]ShaderMaterial[/k] and set the [k]Shader[/k] to your .gdshader script.

Under the [k]Render[/k] properties, go to [k]Film > Transparent[/k] and enable it (Image 1). Go to [k]Color Management[/k] and check the [k]View[/k] setting. Use [k]Standard[/k] if you want a flat, literal 1:1 reproduction of your actual color values — correct for UI/icon work where you want exact color fidelity; otherwise if you want a cinematic scene rendering use [k]Filmic[/k] or [k]AgX[/k].
The render will render everything within the camera viewport, even if you have it hidden. Move everything out of the way of the camera so they don't affect the background transparency.
